content.p: This Act may be cited as the Customs Amendment (Australian Trusted Trader Programme) Act 2015.

section.heading: Obligations under this Part may be satisfied in accordance with a trusted trader agreement

content.p: An entity is released from an obligation that the entity would otherwise be required to satisfy under a provision of this Part (other than Division 1) if the obligation:
is of a kind prescribed by rules for the purposes of Part XA; and
is specified in those rules as an obligation from which an entity may be released; and
is specified in a trusted trader agreement between the Comptroller-General of Customs and the entity.
If:
an obligation must be satisfied under a provision of this Part (other than Division 1); and
the obligation:
is of a kind prescribed by rules for the purposes of Part XA; and
is specified in those rules as an obligation that may be satisfied in a way other than required by this Part; and
is specified in a trusted trader agreement between the Comptroller-General of Customs and an entity;
then, despite the relevant provision, the entity may satisfy the obligation in the way specified in the trusted trader agreement.

section.heading: Establishment of the Australian Trusted Trader Programme

content.p: The Comptroller-General of Customs may, in accordance with this Part, establish a programme to provide trade facilitation benefits to entities.
The programme is to be known as the Australian Trusted Trader Programme.
Subdivision A—Assessment of qualification criteria based on documentary evidence

section.heading: Trusted trader agreement may be entered into

content.p: (1) The Comptroller-General of Customs may enter into an agreement (a trusted trader agreement) with an entity if:
the entity nominates itself to participate in the Australian Trusted Trader Programme; and
the Comptroller-General of Customs considers that it is reasonably likely that the entity will satisfy the qualification criteria set out in the rules.
In deciding whether to enter into a trusted trader agreement, the Comptroller-General of Customs must consider:
any matter set out in the rules; and
any other matter that he or she considers relevant.
If a trusted trader agreement is entered into with an entity:
the agreement confers interim trusted trader status on the entity; and
the entity may receive benefits of a kind prescribed by the rules and specified in the agreement.
A nomination to participate in the Australian Trusted Trader Programme may be made by an entity by document or electronically.
A documentary nomination must:
be communicated to the Comptroller-General of Customs; and
be in an approved form; and
contain the information required by the approved form; and
be signed in a manner indicated by the approved form.
An electronic nomination must communicate such information as is set out in an approved statement.
Subdivision B—Validation of qualification criteria based on physical inspection and audit

section.heading: Variation of a trusted trader agreement

content.p: This section applies if:
a trusted trader agreement is entered into with an entity; and
the Comptroller-General of Customs is satisfied that the entity satisfies the qualification criteria set out in the rules.
The Comptroller-General of Customs may vary a trusted trader agreement to provide for:

the entity to be released from an obligation, of a kind prescribed by the rules and specified in the agreement, that the entity would otherwise be required to satisfy under Part IV (other than Division 1) or Part VI (other than Division 1); or

the entity to satisfy an obligation, of a kind prescribed by the rules and specified in the agreement, that the entity would otherwise be required to satisfy under Part IV (other than Division 1) or Part VI (other than Division 1) in a way specified in the agreement.
Note: Parts IV and VI deal with the importation and the exportation of goods, respectively.
The Comptroller-General of Customs may vary a trusted trader agreement to provide for benefits of a kind prescribed by the rules and specified in the agreement.
In deciding whether to vary a trusted trader agreement, the Comptroller-General of Customs must consider:
any matter set out in the rules; and
any other matter that he or she considers relevant.
If a trusted trader agreement is varied:
the agreement confers ongoing trusted trader status on the entity; and
the entity may receive benefits of a kind prescribed by the rules and specified in the agreement.
Subdivision C—General provisions relating to trusted trader agreements

section.heading: Terms and conditions of trusted trader agreements

content.p: A trusted trader agreement may be subject to:
conditions prescribed by the rules; and
terms and conditions specified in the agreement.

section.heading: Variation, suspension or termination of trusted trader agreements

content.p: The Comptroller-General of Customs may vary, suspend or terminate a trusted trader agreement if the Comptroller-General of Customs reasonably believes that the entity to which the agreement relates has not complied, or is not complying, with:
any condition prescribed by the rules; or
any term or condition specified in the agreement.
In deciding whether to vary, suspend or terminate a trusted trader agreement, the Comptroller-General of Customs must consider:
any matter set out in the rules; and
any other matter that he or she considers relevant.
If subsection (1) applies, the trusted trader agreement must be varied, suspended or terminated in accordance with the procedure prescribed by the rules.

The Comptroller-General of Customs may maintain a register, to be known as the Register of Trusted Trader Agreements, containing information of a kind prescribed by the rules in relation to each trusted trader agreement entered into under this Part.
The Register of Trusted Trader Agreements is to be made publicly available.
The Register of Trusted Trader Agreements is not a legislative instrument.
The Comptroller-General of Customs may, by legislative instrument, prescribe rules for and in relation to the following:
the qualification criteria in relation to which a trusted trader agreement may be:
entered into under section 176A; or
varied under section 177;
the matters that the Comptroller-General of Customs must consider when deciding whether to:
enter into a trusted trader agreement under section 176A; or
vary the agreement under section 177;
the conditions on which an entity participates in the Australian Trusted Trader Programme;
the kind of obligation:
that an entity may be released from under Part IV (other than Division 1) or Part VI (other than Division 1); or
that an entity may be required to satisfy under Part IV (other than Division 1) or Part VI (other than Division 1) in a way other than required by the relevant Part;
the kind of benefits that an entity may receive under a trusted trader agreement;
any criteria to be satisfied for an entity to receive benefits of a kind mentioned in paragraph (e);
any other conditions to which a trusted trader agreement may be subject;
the procedures that the Comptroller-General of Customs must follow when varying, suspending or terminating a trusted trader agreement under section 178A;
the matters that the Comptroller-General of Customs must consider when deciding whether to vary, suspend or terminate a trusted trader agreement under section 178A;
the kinds of information that may be published on the Register of Trusted Trader Agreements, including:
that an entity has entered into a trusted trader agreement; and
whether the agreement confers interim or ongoing trusted trader status on the entity; and
the kinds of benefits that the entity is receiving, or will receive, under the agreement; and
whether the agreement is in force; and
whether the agreement is or has been suspended; and
whether the agreement has been terminated.
For the purpose of paragraph (1)(d):
a rule prescribed for the purposes of subparagraph (1)(d)(i) must specify that the obligation is one from which an entity may be released; and

a rule prescribed for the purposes of subparagraph (1)(d)(ii) must specify that the obligation is one that may be satisfied by an entity in a way other than required by Part IV (other than Division 1) or Part VI (other than Division 1).
The Comptroller-General of Customs may, by legislative instrument, also make rules prescribing matters:
required or permitted by this Part to be prescribed by the rules; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Part.
To avoid doubt, rules made under this section may not do the following:
create an offence or civil penalty;
provide powers of:
arrest or detention; or
entry, search or seizure;
impose a tax;
set an amount to be appropriated from the Consolidated Revenue Fund under an appropriation in this Act;
directly amend the text of this Act.
